input.summary:
room-21 (east upper corridor and wing passage) now builds nothing. Its furniture, carpet and lanterns were all refused (32 of 32) because the shell claims every upper-floor interior air cell, so no free cell existed to move them to.
parts/room-21.mjs no longer writes into earlier parts' cells; the header keeps the design intent and explains the block. Rerunning make.sh shows no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE line for this part, and build.nbt is written.
The part is not built: the furniture is missing until the shell or build.mjs releases these air cells.
left: Room-21 furniture is not built. Its layout was removed from the file. Recover it from the pre-edit version: barrel/chest run on z51 at x56..62 and x68 (y11, chest facing south); dark_oak_fence at x59..60 z51 (y11) with dark_oak_slab type top at y12; flower_pot (59,13,51) and standing lantern (60,13,51); red_carpet z52 x54..67 (y11); hanging lanterns at y16: (53,52), (58,52), (63,52), (67,52), (53,55), (53,59).

Root cause is upstream, outside this file: parts/shell.mjs box() fills the upper-floor interior with air, and runParts counts those air writes as owned. To unblock, either the shell stops claiming these air cells, or the room-21 entry in build.mjs PARTS gets { carve: true } (the carve path lets a part cut owned air that has air above or below; walls stay refused). I did not edit either file.

Out of scope, seen in the same make run: roof.json has off-palette blocks (tuff_brick_slab x258, tuff_bricks x176, cobbled_deepslate_stairs x259, tuff_brick_stairs x228, cobbled_deepslate_slab x285, polished_deepslate_slab x114, polished_deepslate_stairs x122, stone_brick_slab x46). Not touched here.
Other room parts also reported 0 placed in the same run. I did not open them, so I have not checked whether they are stubs or are blocked the same way.

waste.cost: About 4 tool calls and several minutes of reading source, all to explain one refusal class.
waste.tool: runParts should name the owning part and call on each refusal (e.g. 'owned by shell: box() air'), and a preflight should flag a part whose whole footprint is owned before make runs.

waste.what: Tallied the 32 attempted writes by hand from the layers() rows to confirm every one was refused, not only the 8 sample cells.
waste.cost: Hand count over four layers() calls; no code written.
waste.tool: A dry-run mode for a part (or mcd plan on a part) that lists which writes would be refused and which cells are free, plus a total.

waste.what: Could not tell a stub part (writes nothing) from a finished one in the make output, since other rooms also print '0 placed' with no refusals.
waste.cost: Not measured; I did not open the other room parts.
waste.tool: The make report should mark parts with zero writes as stubs, and the room checklist should count placed blocks against the plan.

companions.task: Fit out the upper east corridor once the shell releases its interior air: the linen run, console, carpet runner and hanging lanterns at the coordinates listed in left.
Review what the shell carved to air on the upper floor (box() and the partition lines), so the fit-out sits on finished walls and ceilings instead of being refused by the lock.
